title: Battle of Trebia
summary: Hold the river line and break all three Roman crossings. Let the cold and the water do the work Sempronius will not.
teaching_goal: An assault walks toward your camp but turns for whatever it can see. Bait it with something visible and it will take the ground you chose instead of the ground it wanted.
narrative_intent: The Romans are baited into the winter river and punished by Mago's concealed force, then the defense becomes an assault on a complete winter camp.
historical_context: December 218 BC: Hannibal provoked Tiberius Sempronius Longus into crossing the cold Trebia before breakfast. Carthaginian infantry, cavalry, elephants, and Mago's hidden detachment struck the exhausted Roman army from front, flanks, and rear.

victory_conditions.description: Hold the southern bank through all three crossings. Sempronius spends his army on the ice; you have only to still be standing.
Kill every enemy commander. A nation dies with the man who leads it: its camps fall neutral, its works come down and its troops leave the field.

defeat_conditions.description: Lose the river camp and the cold takes what the Romans couldn't.
Every soldier lost is counted by the enemy tonight.
The commander falls — and every line collapses behind him.
A general alone on a dead field is just the last corpse standing.

optional_objectives.description: Break three Roman columns before the survivors find the ford again.

stages.title: Break the three crossings
stages.description: Hold the southern bank through every Roman assault phase.
stages.hint: Sempronius spends his army on the ice; you only have to still be standing.

stages.title: Kill Sempronius and his officers
stages.description: Ride down the commanders once the crossings break.
stages.hint: The winter camp lies north across the river.

actions.text: Hold discipline. Let the Romans commit at the ford.
Roman reserves are moving from the western bank.
Counterattack now. Break them while they are split by the river.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: Cold water and an early start, and my colleague is very pleased with both. He has the men in the river before their porridge. I said what I thought and was overruled, so I shall stand here and watch your ambush do its arithmetic.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: Fine. Sempronius rides to Rome to explain his morning. Half a legion walked out of that water and kept walking, and they will meet you again in the spring with dry feet and long memories.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: The river keeps whatever it is given. Your elephants went in and not all of them came out, and the Trebia is not a large river. Rome has never needed a large one.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: Sempronius is crossing. Now, in the cold, without breakfast, because a consul's year ends in March and he wants his battle before it does.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: The last of the legions is in the water. Everything Rome has north of the Apennines is coming at you wet. Hold this and you hold Italy for a winter.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: The western reserve is moving, against my advice. I gave the advice knowing it would be ignored; it is still worth having given.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: We are on your bank and at your works. A river only stops men who are not already freezing.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: Your line is bleeding along the bank. Wet ground is slow ground, and slow men are what spears are for.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: Hannibal is down in the Trebia mud. Whatever Mago has hidden in the gullies, it will not bring him back.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: Sempronius has a handful left and they are on the wrong side of a winter river. He will still call it a victory in Rome. He always does.

theme: Freezing water, fog, and exhaustion turn the Roman advance into a ritual slaughter.
